summary: MEM Finder is an interactive web app that finds and ranks places on Earth that look and behave like the Moon and Mars. Space agencies test rovers, habitats and astronaut training in these “terrestrial analogs”, but picking good ones is slow and scattered across many datasets. MEM Finder pulls open NASA, ESA, CSA and JAXA data into one place. It gives each Earth site a 0-100 similarity score against a lunar or Martian target, based on terrain and geology, climate, resources, operations and data quality. You explore everything on 3D Earth, Moon and Mars globes, with matching Moon/Mars counterpart coordinates and a small simulation. It matters because better analogs mean cheaper, safer testing before real missions. It also highlights lesser-known sites, such as Hingol and Kharan in Pakistan, that deserve global attention.
details:
What it does
MEM Finder lets you pick a Moon or Mars landing site and instantly see which Earth locations are its best match. Each analog gets a weighted similarity score (0-100) shown as a map layer and on rotating 3D globes of Earth, Moon and Mars. Markers link every Earth site to its off-world counterpart coordinates. A small simulation lets you compare conditions side by side.

How the scoring works
We score five factor groups:

  • Terrain and geology (30%)
  • Temperature and climate (20%)
  • Resources (20%)
  • Operations and access
  • Data quality

Weights are adjustable, so a rover team and a habitat team can each rank sites by what matters to them.

Analog sites included

  • Mars analogs: Hingol and Kharan Desert (Pakistan), Dasht-e Lut (Iran), Dalangtan/Qaidam Basin (China), Samail Ophiolite (Oman)
  • Moon analogs: Lonar Crater (India), Chagai/Koh-e-Taftan (Pakistan), Mount Suswa (Kenya), Pinacate (Mexico), Teide/Las Cañadas (Tenerife)

Data sources

  • NASA Earthdata Search and Worldview
  • PDS and LRO Diviner (Moon and Mars surface data)
  • CSA RCM and RADARSAT-1
  • Copernicus Data Space
  • JAXA G-Portal
  • Terrain: SRTM, Copernicus DEM, USGS 3DEP
  • Aridity: NASA POWER, WorldClim, CHIRPS
  • Temperature: POWER, ERA5, MODIS LST
  • Volcanic: USGS and GVP
  • Polar: NSIDC and ArcticDEM

Tools
A web app built with an AI app builder, with interactive 3D globes and a map-based visualization layer.

Benefits and impact

  • Saves mission planners time by putting scattered open data in one tool
  • Makes analog testing cheaper and more accessible, since teams can find sites closer to home
  • Brings attention to under-studied analog regions, especially in South and Central Asia
  • Open data only, so anyone can verify and reuse the results

Creativity
Instead of a static list of analog sites, MEM Finder is a visual, explorable tool. Moon, Mars and Earth sit side by side, and the similarity score updates with the user’s priorities.

Factors we considered
Data availability and resolution, how well each Earth site really matches off-world conditions, accessibility and safety for field testing, and keeping the scoring transparent and adjustable.
dataRefs: Where Is the Hottest Place on Earth?
